item.title: Earthquake of 2.8 shakes northern Groningen
item.description:
Earthquake of 2.8 shakes northern Groningen

August 21, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

An earthquake measuring 2.8 on the Richter scale struck the north of Groningen in the early hours of Friday, the heaviest to hit the region since March.

The epicentre was near the village of Zandeweer, in the Het Hogeland area, at a depth of three kilometres, the meteorological agency KNMI said. The quake was recorded at around 5.50am local time.

Residents in the nearby villages of Uithuizen, Kantens, Rottum and Middelstum said they had felt the tremor, broadcaster NOS reported. No damage or injuries had been reported by Friday morning.

The KNMI classed the quake as an “induced earthquake”, meaning it was caused by gas extraction. Tremors linked to drilling tend to occur closer to the surface, making them easier to feel; those measuring 1.5 and above are noticeable.

Extraction from the main Groningen field stopped two years ago, but the KNMI has warned that quakes can continue for decades as the ground settles. Gas is still being pumped from smaller fields in the province, where drilling is permitted until the end of 2032.

The last comparable tremor was a 3.0 quake near Eleveld in Drenthe in March. The strongest of the 31 induced quakes recorded near the Groningen field last year was a 3.4 tremor at Zeerijp in November, among the heaviest ever measured in the province.

item.title: Bruls calls on justice ministry to enforce motorway tractor ban
item.description:
Bruls calls on justice ministry to enforce motorway tractor ban

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Local politicians have called for nationwide rules to be enforced to keep tractors off motorways in the wake of a fatal crash during a farmers’ protest a week ago.

Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the board of regional safety councils, said it was “incomprehensible” that local authorities took different approaches to enforcing the traffic rules.

Last Friday two people died in a collision on the A59 at the tail end of a queue that had built up on the A59 near Hees, a suburb of Nijmegen.

Police and the prosecution service had said before the collision happened that they would not prosecute farmers who drove tractors onto the motorway, even though they are prohibited, citing the right to demonstrate.

The prosecution service has since said that anyone who drives a tractor onto the motorway will be subject to enforcement, even though police said at an earlier demonstration that they did not have enough evidence to go on because the farmers had taped over their numberplates.

Bruls told NOS he wanted to hold talks with the justice ministry to decide on a national strategy for offences on the motorway.

“It’s not manageable for the police if every mayor comes up with their own guidelines and the rules change every 10 or 15 kilometres. Some things should be agreed at a regional level.

“For motorways we need to have a national approach because the motorway network covers the whole country.”

Prime minister Rob Jetten said following last week’s deadly crash it was “unacceptable” for farm vehicles to be on motorways. “It leads to very dangerous situations,” he said.

item.title: Max Verstappen signs Red Bull extension on eve of Dutch GP
item.description:
Max Verstappen signs Red Bull extension on eve of Dutch GP

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Four-time Formula One world champion Max Verstappen has signed an extended contract with Red Bull Racing, ending speculation that he could leave the team or quit the sport altogether.

Verstappen, 28, was rumoured to be contemplating a move to rivals McLaren or Mercedes in recent months, but in a press release on Thursday he said he had chosen to stay with the team he saw as a “second family”.

”We have the best people and I’m excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again,” he said. “This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue.”

He dismissed reports he had been in talks behind the scenes about a possible move to McLaren next season. “I was closer to quitting than changing teams,” he said.

The news that Verstappen will keep driving for Red Bull until 2030 will be welcomed by Dutch fans on the eve of the last edition of his home Grand Prix this weekend.

“To make this announcement during the last Grand Prix at Zandvoort is a great moment for me as well,” Verstappen said. “Hopefully we can give the fans a special send-off for the final race.”

Hybrid cars

Verstappen won the first three races after Zandvoort returned to the Formula One calendar in 2021, at a time when he dominated the sport, winning 71 races in 10 years and four consecutive world titles between 2021 and 2024.

This year he is standing sixth in the championship race, 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, and is yet to record a win.

Verstappen has criticised the new hybrid cars introduced this season, that require drivers to save on fuel by recharging the battery during the race, describing them as “not fun to drive” and “anti-racing”.

Earlier this season he took part in the 24-hour race at the Nürburgring in Germany. Verstappen said being able to drive more endurance races in future years was “one of the factors and wishes” that influenced his decision to sign a new deal.

He was also caught up in the tensions within the Red Bull team surrounding the departure of former team boss Christian Horner, who left just over a year ago after being accused of sexually harassing a female colleague.

Horner was twice cleared of wrongdoing, but left with a £52 mln (€60 mln) payout amid accusations by Verstappen’s father, Jos, that he was “driving people apart”. Horner later said Max Verstappen played no role in his departure.

item.title: Prosecutors link three more deaths to drugs sold on internet
item.description:
Prosecutors link three more deaths to drugs sold on internet

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch prosecutors say they have linked three more deaths to drugs bought on the Dutch-run Funcaps website, bringing the total number to 21.

Jord van W. and Stefan P., aged 31 and 30 and both from Limburg, have been charged with earning millions of euros from the sale of fake tranquilisers and sleeping pills, which are usually only available on prescription, as well as designer drugs.

The duo, who didn’t have a license to sell medicines, were closed down and sentenced in April by a Belgium court to three years in prison, including a year and a half suspended, for the illegal trafficking of medicines and drugs.

But they continued to trade in the Netherlands, where they achieved sales of €42 million in five years. They were arrested in August last year along with a third man, Van W.’s brother, who has been released but remains a suspect.

Prosecutors told a court in Zwolle that three more people had been identified who had died after taking drugs sold on Funcaps, while another two deaths are being investigated.

The website offered free gifts for large orders as well as a discount scheme and described its illegal medicines collection as “research chemicals”. They came with no usage information.

The website also sold sex toys, smoking tools and smart drugs, promising “discreet packaging” to clients.

“We did not foresee that a causal connection would be found in so many cases,” they said.

Many of the victims were “young people in the prime of their lives,” Zwolle judges heard. “That’s what makes this case so serious and unique.”

The next hearing is scheduled for November.

item.title: Thunderstorm and tornado warnings as Dutch summer heatwave ends
item.description:
Thunderstorm and tornado warnings as Dutch summer heatwave ends

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Coastal provinces could be hit by heavy rain, hail and even tornadoes on Thursday afternoon as the hot, dry summer weather in the Netherlands comes to an abrupt halt.

The meteorological institute KNMI has issued a code yellow warning for all coastal provinces, from Groningen to Zeeland, including the Wadden Islands.

The agency has warned people in the area to expect heavy showers, hail and gusts of up to 60 km/h. Tornadoes have already been spotted off the coast.

The warnings for hail and thunderstorms are in place until 5pm for Groningen and Friesland and until 6pm in other coastal areas, where tornadoes are forecast.

Heavy showers and storms are expected to continue through Friday, especially in the IJsselmeer region, with temperatures reaching 19 or 20 degrees in the daytime. Nights will be much cooler at between 10 and 14 degrees.

The best of the weekend weather will be on Sunday, with more sunshine and temperatures of up to 21 degrees.

item.title: Mortgages rise as first-time homebuyers take out more loans
item.description:
Mortgages rise as first-time homebuyers take out more loans

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The number of mortgages taken out by Dutch homeowners in the first half of the year has gone up to €84.8 bn, with more first-time buyers getting on the ladder.

That was less than the record in the second half of 2025 but 8% higher than in the first half of 2025.

The latest figures show that more young people are taking out starter loans on top of their mortgages, which help them bridge the financial gap between the price of their home and the amount they are allowed to borrow as first-time buyers.

Loans were taken out on 8.3% of all starter home mortgages, up from 6.4% during the first half of 2025.

Starter loans, which are now offered to first-time buyers in more than 300 out of the 342 Dutch municipalities, proved especially popular with people up to the age of 25. Some 15% of this group obtained a starter loan in the first half of this year, compared to 8.6% of people between 25 and 35 years old.

The average amount borrowed was about € 37,000, up from €35,700 last year.

item.title: Three Dutch men killed in minibus crash during holiday in US
item.description:
Three Dutch men killed in minibus crash during holiday in US

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Three Dutch nationals have died when a minibus collided with a tractor trailer in the US state of Ohio.

According to US media, the van carrying seven people was driven by Dutchman Gijs M. Odpam, 48, who apparently failed to yield at a stop sign in Knox County and was then struck by the tractor trailer.

Three men died at the scene of Tuesday’s collision: Arno Kramer, 55, Martijn E. Van Vooren, 44, and Hermanus J. Fortuin, 55.

The driver and three other passengers, all of whom were from the Netherlands, were taken to local hospitals. The extent of their injuries has not been disclosed.

The Dutch foreign ministry called the incident “a terrible accident” and sent staff from other regions in the US to Ohio to aid the victims and their families.

The Dutch nationals are said to be part of a travel group of 16 people who were divided between two vans. It’s unknown where the other van was at the time of the accident, which is still under investigation.

item.title: Gangs suspected of stealing fire station equipment for ram-raids
item.description:
Gangs suspected of stealing fire station equipment for ram-raids

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

More than 60 fire stations have been targeted in the last year by criminal gangs who steal hydraulic equipment to use in ram raids.

One fire station in Sassenheim, near Leiden in Zuid-Holland, was attacked three nights in a row in the last week, while 10 sites have been broken into across the country in the last fortnight.

Police told NRC the thieves were looking for equipment such as cutting gear and hydraulic jacks used to free people who are trapped beneath rubble.

The machines can be repurposed to break heavily fortified windows used by shops such as jewellers and electrical retailers. Last week thieves left behind a hydraulic spreader that they used to try to smash the window of a jewellery store in Den Bosch.

The number of break-ins has jumped in the last year, with just 18 thefts from fire stations recorded in 2025 and 17 the year before.

“We are trying to strengthen our response teams and making detecting these crimes a national priority,” police spokesman Dick Goijert said.

Safety boards would not say exactly what was taken in the most recent raids because the police investigation is ongoing and to avoid giving “unnecessary information to people with bad intentions”.

Accessibility issues

Fire station managers have tried to improve security, but locking away life-saving equipment means it takes longer to retrieve it in an emergency, when a few lost seconds can make the difference between life and death.

Evert Jansen, a former burglar who now works for the police to raise companies’ awareness of the need to improve security, said he suspected organised criminals were behind the thefts.

“Unless they know how the equipment works it’s difficult for them to use it,” Jansen told NRC. “Maybe the burglars are stealing it on the orders of experienced criminals.”

item.title: Community remembers 17-year-old Lisa, but safety concerns remain
item.description:
Community remembers 17-year-old Lisa, but safety concerns remain

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Exactly a year ago, 17-year-old Lisa was stabbed to death while cycling home to Abcoude after a night out in Amsterdam, sending shockwaves through the country and spearheading campaigns to combat violence against women.

Lisa’s body was found beside a cycleway in Duivendrecht, between the city and her home town, where she was pulled from her bike and stabbed to death while she was on the phone to police.

Shortly afterwards, a 22-year-old Nigerian man known as Christ Jude was arrested at a nearby Amsterdam refugee centre. Earlier this year, he confessed to killing Lisa, along with the rape and attempted rape of two other women in Amsterdam.

A memorial organised by a village church and youth centre will take place in Abcoude Thursday, where people can leave notes or light a candle for Lisa.

Family thanks

That community support, said Lisa’s family in a recent letter thanking Abcoude’s residents, has given them the “the security and strength to resume our lives step by step”.

“Not by hiding us, but by continuing with everything that was so dear to Lisa. Let’s laugh, dance, toast and celebrate life as Lisa did—full of dedication, with a generous smile and surrounded by friends,” they said.

Lisa’s murder took place during the Abcoude Festive Week (Feestweek Abcoude), a five-day annual festival that this year will be held from August 25-29. Organisers have consulted with Lisa’s family, and a commemorative event is expected to be included in the programme. The family’s letter thanking fellow villagers will also be distributed in the program’s booklet.

“It is almost unbelievable that it will soon be a year since Lisa passed away. Our world collapsed and the impact on the town was also immense,” reads the letter. “Thanks to all the villagers for the impressive minutes of silence we were able to experience together. Thank you for the hedge of honour you formed during the funeral, we will never forget these moments.”

Moving forward

Since the murder rattled the country and led to national soul-searching on how to protect women from violence, some things have changed.

Municipalities have taken to designing safer public spaces with women in mind, with several adding more lighting and pruning back shrubbery for more visibility.

But for Danique de Jong, it’s not enough. She organized a “We Claim the Night” crowd-funding campaign shortly after the murder that raised more than half a million euro in three days, money that has been spent on policy, education and victim assistance.

“Many of these measures are about reducing the feeling of insecurity: mowing bushes and setting up a lamp. Then we feel safer, but it doesn’t make us safer,” de Jong told RTV Utrecht. “If we only focus on pepper spray, pruning bunches and hanging lighting, nothing will change.”

Mostly at home

While she said she’s hopeful and applauds the changes, she calls for a cultural shift regarding violence against women. “4.5 million girls in the Netherlands had to deal with sexual violence before the age of 18…[with] someone in their environment who does not accept ‘no’”.

That’s because violence against women mostly occurs closer to home. “A girl being murdered by an unknown person or man is very disturbing but doesn’t happen very often,” Roos Koolhof, a healthcare psychologist who works with victims and those at risk of sexual assault for Levvel/Qpido, told Dutch News at the time of Lisa’s murder.

“Mostly assaults happen in a familiar atmosphere—86% of the time—by the neighbour or your stepfather or a boyfriend or a friend or someone they meet on social media.

“What happens more often is a slap on the ass or touching someone somewhere they don’t like,” she says. “And that is what we should talk about so it won’t happen anymore.”

A survey by the youth news program NOS Stories found that many women feel unsafe in certain places and often carry keys to protect themselves against attack.

Christ Jude’s trial is expected to start in Amsterdam in January.

item.title: More permits issued for newbuilds but pipeline is filling up
item.description:
More permits issued for newbuilds but pipeline is filling up

August 20, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Turnover in the construction trade was up by 5.2% in the second quarter of 2026 while the number of newbuild permits was close to record levels, continuing the strong trend of the last 18 months.

Sales have grown by at least 5% in every three-month period but one since the end of 2024, although the market has cooled off from its peak of more than 7% aa year ago.

Newbuild permits issued in May, the latest month for which figures are available, stood at 10,824 for domestic houses and 2,637 commercial properties. The total figure is the highest since December 2024, when more than 13,600 permits were issued, statistics agency CBS said.

The number of buildings in the pipeline grew to nearly 234,000 houses and 48,000 commercial premises.

Permits are being issued faster than buildings are being completed, which has caused the pipeline figure to grow by around 33% for houses and 25% for business premises in the last two and a half years.

The CBS also recorded a steep growth in costs in the construction sector, with a 97% increase for domestic properties in the last year.

The agency said the spike was partly caused by congestion on the electricity network, which had prompted councils to speed up the planning process for newbuild projects before restrictions on new connections kicked in.

The labour market in the sector remains tight, with 28,600 unfilled vacancies recorded by the CBS. In the second quarter of the year 133 construction companies folded, five more than in the winter months.
